chapter: South America and back in New York
title: Turning down the Cotton Club for the Ufa Palast
summary: The band votes for Berlin's Ufa Palast rather than go back to Harlem, a decision Wooding still thinks was right because Duke Ellington's jungle sound suited the club.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: He said, 'Anyhow.' But As thing come on. So we were working in vaudeville at the time and I got this cablegram from Europe to come to the Ufe Palace if I wanted to. And they said the money was good and we had a powow and that was about the same chance I had to go -- the Cotton Club was opening. So we all had a powow, and we decided to take the Ufe Palace, because the Cotton Club was just starting in Harlem and -some of them been born- we had all been born in Harlem and others been living there all their life, and so we said, 'Well, what do we want to go back to Harlem for?' We've been on Broadway, we've been in Berlin, we've been in London, we've been in Paris, and all over the world. Now, we go back to Harlem, for what?' But we couldn't see into the future. We couldn't see that later on it was going to be the greatest club of all of them, see? And so we turned the offer down.
Do you think, now, looking back, that it would have been wise for you to stay? Have stayed?
No, I don't. I still don't. Because I don't think that anyone would have done as well as Duke did.

For the simple reason why, I think our music was on too high a plane for it. See Duke came in and his band played what they called 'jungle music'. They were built on the style of Bubba Nisky. And that was the people in that place were Beer Barons, and all like that. They could stand it. When I was down in the Club Alabam, they wouldn't allow us to beat four beats out.
